transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on SSO (SAML) + SCIM provisioning patterns and to build an entitlement matrix for least-privilege RBAC across Atlas Biologics teams. Heavy focus on audit logs, KMS/BYOK concerns, EU/US data residency, and a short plan for a SCIM test sync.

Topics covered:
- SAML metadata and IdP requirements
- SCIM attribute and group mapping
- RBAC roles and entitlement matrix sprint
- Audit log export and retention
- Encryption at rest & KMS (BYOK vs Redwood-managed)
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)

Action items (recap): see action_items field above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh — I see Priya, Marcus, Lena and Tom on the call. We'll do a quick agenda run, then Diego will walk through some RBAC patterns and then we can map to your SCIM attributes.
[00:16] Dr. Priya Shah: Yep thanks Samira. We wanna make sure this is, um, low friction for the app teams and that we don't overprovision. Our compliance team — Lena — wants to limit admin blast radius.
[00:30] Lena O'Neal: Yeah, hi. Also need to validate audit trails for HIPAA-ish workloads, though we aren't officially a covered entity. We still need long retention for some ephys logs.
[00:44] Diego Ramos: Cool. High-level, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM v2 for provisioning. There are a couple of common patterns: direct SCIM push for group membership, or JIT group mapping via SAML assertion if your IdP includes groups. We usually recommend SCIM for enterprise provisioning.
[01:04] Marcus Wynn: Quick question — our IdP is Okta and we use SCIM for other SaaS. What's the expected attribute set? We have employeeType, department, manager, custom:atlas-role.
[01:18] Diego Ramos: Perfect, Okta is supported. For RBAC mapping, we prefer group-based entitlements: map Okta groups like atlas-admins, atlas-ops, atlas-billing to Redwood roles. SCIM attributes we look for: userName, emails, active, displayName, externalId and group membership. Custom attributes are fine — can map custom:atlas-role to a fine-grained permission if you need.
[01:38] Dr. Priya Shah: Is there a recommended naming convention? We have inconsistent group names currently.
[01:44] Samira Patel: We can share a role mapping template. Diego will produce an entitlement matrix CSV that shows proposed Redwood roles — Admin, Operator, Billing, Viewer, and Service — and example Okta groups to map. Also include token scopes for CI uses.
[02:02] Diego Ramos: I'll add a 'service' role for machine account tokens and recommend using short-lived tokens with rotation, plus audit logging for all token creation.
[02:12] Tom Becker: About the tokens — can we do key rotation via our KMS? We prefer BYOK where possible.
[02:20] Aisha Khan: Short answer: yes, for Private deployments we have BYOK/HSM integrations. For Hosted API we offer Redwood-managed KMS with optional customer-managed keys in dedicated/private. There's sometimes a cap on BYOK in multi-tenant envs, Diego maybe add detail.
[02:40] Diego Ramos: Right, for Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private you can bring your own key and we integrate with common KMSes (AWS KMS on AWS regions, Azure Key Vault on Azure, and HSM options for on-prem). For Hosted we can do a dedicated CMK for enterprise customers on contracts, but full BYOK with hardware-backed HSM is generally on Private.
[02:58] Marcus Wynn: Ok good. How is data encrypted at rest and in transit? We need details for our security review.
[03:06] Samira Patel: In transit TLS 1.2+ (TLS1.3 where possible). At rest we use AES-256. The model artifacts and logs in Dedicated/Private can be stored in customer-owned buckets if desired. We'll send architecture and network diagram.
[03:23] Lena O'Neal: About logs — we need to ship audit logs to our Splunk instance and keep them for 7 years for certain regulated projects. Feasible?
[03:34] Diego Ramos: We have an audit-log export pipeline; you can push syslog/HTTPS to your SIEM. Retention isn't a problem on your side; we'll export raw events and you can archive in Splunk or S3. Need to confirm event types and retention SLA.
[03:50] Dr. Priya Shah: What about PII in logs? We can't have full request payloads in the logs.
[03:58] Samira Patel: Good flag. We can filter and redact PII from logs. The default audit event includes metadata: actor, action, resource id, timestamp, and reference IDs. Payloads with user content are not stored in plain logs in Hosted by default; for Dedicated/Private you can control exact log policies.
[04:20] Marcus Wynn: Data residency — we must ensure model requests from EU patients stay in EU; can Redwood pin regionally per project?
[04:29] Diego Ramos: Yes, routing policies can pin requests to region — EU/US/APAC — and we can restrict model variants to be hosted in EU-only. For Private you can fully control the infra. For Hosted we do regional tenancy but need to put that in the SLA.
[04:45] Tom Becker: Onboard process: we want a small sprint to build the entitlement matrix and then run a SCIM sync into a test tenant. Proposed timeline?
[04:54] Samira Patel: I propose: Diego delivers the mapping template by Thursday (11/19), Marcus and Tom share IdP metadata and group names by Monday (11/20), then schedule a 1-hour SCIM test (11/23–11/27 window). After successful sync we run a short smoke test for RBAC.
[05:12] Lena O'Neal: Sounds good. On the RBAC model, we also require separation of duties for admin and billing — they cannot overlap. Can we enforce that in the role assignments?
[05:22] Diego Ramos: Yes, the entitlement matrix will indicate conflicts and we'll attach guardrails. We can enforce via group membership and also flag in console UI where a user is in conflicting groups.
[05:32] Dr. Priya Shah: A couple of compliance questions: do you have SOC 2 Type II? ISO 27001? How often are audits?
[05:40] Samira Patel: We have SOC 2 Type II with coverage for Hosted and Dedicated controls — I will send the report. We completed ISO 27001 in 2025 and surveillance audits are annual. We'll include evidence and the scope.
[05:54] Marcus Wynn: Does Redwood provide attestations for encryption key handling and separation of duties for ops? We need procedures for key rotation and access logs for KMS.
[06:05] Aisha Khan: We have documented key rotation policies and can include procedure snippets. For Private we give you KMS logs and HSM attestation. For Hosted we can provide rotation cadence and proof of control but not direct HSM access unless in dedicated/private.
[06:20] Tom Becker: For SCIM, if we sync groups to Redwood, what happens on deprovision? Does a disabled user instantly lose access? We need immediate revocation.
[06:29] Diego Ramos: SCIM active=false triggers immediate deprovisioning. Also token revocation APIs exist for sessions and service tokens. We'll recommend short token TTLs (minutes/hours) for high privilege.
[06:42] Dr. Priya Shah: Are there rate limits on SCIM operations? We plan bulk imports.
[06:48] Diego Ramos: SCIM has rate limits on hosted endpoints; for bulk provisioning we can do a CSV import or coordinate a bulk sync in a dedicated window. For Dedicated you have higher throughput.
[06:59] Marcus Wynn: Audit log schema: can you send an event catalog? We want to map to our SIEM fields.
[07:05] Samira Patel: Yes, we'll attach an event catalog. It includes user_id, actor_ip, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, request_id, trace_id, and optional payload refs.
[07:18] Lena O'Neal: Also need proof of encryption at rest for backups and model KV caches — not just object stores.
[07:26] Diego Ramos: Model KV cache encryption is covered; we can provide the encryption design note for runtime caches and intermediate storage.
[07:36] Tom Becker: One more technical detail — when you're talking about region pinning, what about fallbacks? If the EU cluster is down, does it fail open to US? That's a no-go.
[07:47] Diego Ramos: Good point. Our routing policies can set strict regional SLOs with no cross-region fallback for strict data residency projects. Default behavior is fallback but we can configure no-fallback per project in policy.
[08:02] Dr. Priya Shah: Great. Any concerns with our current plan? Marcus?
[08:09] Marcus Wynn: Mostly need the mapping template and the ability to test token revocation and log exports. Also want to validate the KMS integration for service tokens.
[08:19] Samira Patel: Then next steps are clear. We'll share docs and schedule the SCIM test. Diego — you'll draft the entitlement matrix and an example mapping.
[08:29] Diego Ramos: Yep, will do. I'll include examples for group->role mappings, and for service accounts show recommended token scopes and rotation steps.
[08:38] Lena O'Neal: Can Redwood provide a sample SLA clause for data residency and log retention to include in our procurement?
[08:46] Samira Patel: Yes, we have standard contract language for redwood-in-region and log retention. I'll pull the compliance pack and mark the relevant clauses.
[08:56] Tom Becker: We'll also need a short walkthrough of the console to show RBAC enforcement and audit views. Can we do that in the SCIM test session?
[09:03] Diego Ramos: Absolutely, we can do a 20–30 minute demo after a successful sync to show the console audit timeline and role assignment UI.
[09:12] Dr. Priya Shah: Ok, I think that covers it. Anything else?
[09:18] Samira Patel: Quick recap: Samira sends compliance docs by 11/17; Diego sends entitlement matrix by 11/19; Atlas sends IdP metadata by 11/20; schedule SCIM test during 11/23–11/27; confirm Splunk export endpoint by 11/24. I'll follow up in email with calendar invites.
[09:36] Lena O'Neal: Thanks everyone.
[09:38] Marcus Wynn: Thanks.
[09:39] Tom Becker: Thanks.
[09:40] Samira Patel: Thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
